payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: transform the black DVD into a white DVD
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Is the DVD visibly white rather than black in the edited image?
node.criteria: Pass if the DVD is visibly white rather than black; fail if it remains black or is visibly another color; unknown if its color cannot be determined.
node.binding: The DVD identified in the original image; it must remain identifiable as a DVD.

node_traces.evidence: The DVD is visibly white in the edited image.
The DVD is visibly white in the edited image and remains identifiable as a disc.
The DVD is visibly white in the edited image and remains identifiable as a disc.
The DVD is visibly white in the edited image and remains identifiable as a disc.
The DVD is visibly white in the edited image.

fulfillment: The node’s binding is too vague and its traces show a systematic target-association error: the edited image contains two white discs, while the original black DVD is the small rectangular item near the center, not the black animal-like object. The traces repeatedly treat a white disc as the DVD and infer identity from disc shape/center hole, then mark fulfillment complete; that does not establish that the original DVD was transformed. Tighten the binding to track the DVD at its source location and compare that same object across images, requiring evidence that it is the original target before judging color or retained identity. Preserve the rubric’s partial/unresolved distinctions: if the target cannot be matched confidently, do not infer success or no progress. The repeated high-confidence yes outputs are evidence of a binding/evidence failure, not a reason to relax the requested criteria. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is indicated.
s2: Tighten the binding to identify the original DVD by its source location and appearance (the small rectangular item near the image center), then track that same object in the edited image. Do not treat either white disc—especially one over the animal-like object—as proof that the DVD was transformed or retained its identity. Require evidence linking the edited object to the original target before assessing the requested color change or DVD identity. Keep partial and unresolved outcomes available: if the original item cannot be matched, do not infer success or no progress. The repeated high-confidence passes indicate a binding/evidence failure, not a reason to relax the rubric; no transport, schema, or dependency failure is indicated.

The two white discs in the edit are not, by shape or color alone, evidence that the original DVD was transformed.
